title: selenicereus grandiflorus subsp. hondurensis
intro: Selenicereus grandiflorus subsp. hondurensis, commonly known as the Honduran night-blooming cereus, is a species of flowering plant in the family Cactaceae. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antiviral properties, which may help alleviate symptoms of various ailments. The therapeutic actions of Selenicereus grandiflorus subsp. hondurensis are attributed to the presence of bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which have been shown to exhibit antimicrobial, antiparasitic, and anticancer activities. Further research is needed to fully understand the therapeutic potential of this plant and to isolate and characterize its bioactive compounds.
